<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiDB! Please read TiDB's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/pingcap/community/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document **BEFORE** filing this PR.
-->

### What problem does this PR solve? <!--add issue link with summary if exists-->

Fix #14427

### What is changed and how it works?

This PR try to fix a random failed in unit test `TestInfo` in `domain/domain_test.go`.

Before this PR, For testing the case `SchemaSyncer` unexpectedly stop and automatically  restart, we use `failpoint` inject into `syncer.Done()`, but this may cause an unexpected test failed. So in this PR, we remove this `failpoint` and call `syncer.Close()` directly.
Also, because it's hard to detect the state changes of `dom.SchemaValidator.IsStarted()` from `true -> false` and `false -> true`, I remove this check. Even if the check is removed, the code next to `syncer.Close()` will implicit do the check, because without a running `SchemaValidator`, these code cannot run and will throw an error.

The test coverage keep the same.
Before this PR:
```
ok      github.com/pingcap/tidb/domain  0.596s  coverage: 80.3% of statements
```
After this PR:
```
ok      github.com/pingcap/tidb/domain  0.628s  coverage: 80.3% of statements
```

# [Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/pingcap/tidb/pull/15305?src=pr&el=h1) Report
> Merging [#15305](https://codecov.io/gh/pingcap/tidb/pull/15305?src=pr&el=desc) into [master](https://codecov.io/gh/pingcap/tidb/commit/ab17254e3b0a270c6ea4f236d541a8cc8f6f7d39&el=desc) will **not change** coverage by `%`.
> The diff coverage is `n/a`.


```diff
@@             Coverage Diff             @@
##             master     #15305   +/-   ##
===========================================
  Coverage   80.4124%   80.4124%           
===========================================
  Files           502        502           
  Lines        133294     133294           
===========================================
  Hits         107185     107185           
  Misses        17706      17706           
  Partials       8403       8403           
```
Closed, due to it actually does not fix the problem.

I think there may be two issues in this test:
- When the fail-point `ErrorMockSessionDone`  run `s.loadSession().Close()`  and then return `s.loadSession().Done()` these two `s.loadSession()` may refer to different object if `loadSchemaInLoop` loop read from `sync.Done()` first and renew the syncer. Farther more, even if the returned channel is the old one, if the `loadSchemaInLoop` have read the message first, the  `<-dom.ddl.SchemaSyncer().Done()` will also will forever.
- We run in a loop for at most 1s to wait the syncer ready, but maybe 1s isn't enough for the syncer to start if the load is heavy. Or maybe there are other issues.

Maybe we should fix the first issue first?

@glorv 
> When the fail-point ErrorMockSessionDone run s.loadSession().Close() and then return s.loadSession().Done() these two s.loadSession() may refer to different object if loadSchemaInLoop loop read from sync.Done() first and renew the syncer.

This case is rarely happened, but if it happened, the later `loadSession` which in `s.loadSession().Done()` will always get newer object than `s.loadSession().Close()`, The newer object ensure it can restart successfully in some timing.

> if the loadSchemaInLoop have read the message first, the `<-dom.ddl.SchemaSyncer().Done()` will also will forever.

But test failed with `start syncer failed`, that means the line `<-dom.ddl.SchemaSyncer().Done()` has passed, and after the timeout `1s`, the test failed.

> We run in a loop for at most 1s to wait the syncer ready...

Maybe this is the only reason.

> newer

yes, for this issue this is ture. In some time ago, I came across a failure that run test timeout by this case (the timeout backtrace shows), the reason should be what I said.
